entries.meta: Work a system does once, whatever the request, that every later reply reuses: committing to the weights, and a setup run a session reuses.
entries.name: One-time work
entries.terms: one-time work work a system does once, whatever the request, that every later reply reuses: committing to the weights, and a setup run a session reuses.

entries.meta: The organisation that serves a model and generates proofs for it, such as an AI lab or API provider.
entries.name: Operator
entries.terms: operator the organisation that serves a model and generates proofs for it, such as an ai lab or api provider.

entries.meta: Our own execution of a publisher's machine-checked proof using the proof assistant and exact version pinned by the publisher, at the commit we benchmarked.
entries.name: Our rebuild
entries.terms: our rebuild our own execution of a publisher's machine-checked proof using the proof assistant and exact version pinned by the publisher, at the commit we benchmarked.

entries.meta: A system passes on a model when all six of our checks pass.
entries.name: Passed
entries.terms: passed a system passes on a model when all six of our checks pass.

entries.meta: A check passes when its test yields the required result.
entries.name: Passed (check)
entries.terms: passed (check) a check passes when its test yields the required result.

entries.meta: The full Git commit hash at which we build, run, and quote a proof system.
entries.name: Pinned commit
entries.terms: pinned commit the full git commit hash at which we build, run, and quote a proof system.

entries.meta: A cryptographic commitment to a polynomial that lets the prover prove the polynomial's value at any verifier-chosen point using a compact proof.
entries.name: Polynomial commitment
entries.terms: polynomial commitment a cryptographic commitment to a polynomial that lets the prover prove the polynomial's value at any verifier-chosen point using a compact proof.

entries.meta: A ranked system's standing within its model table, equal to 1 plus the number of systems ranked strictly ahead of it.
entries.name: Position
entries.terms: position a ranked system's standing within its model table, equal to 1 plus the number of systems ranked strictly ahead of it.

entries.meta: One of the six entry checks: we modify one prompt token, and the verifier must reject the proof (rule).
entries.name: Prompt check
entries.terms: prompt check one of the six entry checks: we modify one prompt token, and the verifier must reject the proof (rule).

entries.meta: On a system page, the proof file produced for a reply so the verifier can check it.
entries.name: Proof
entries.terms: proof on a system page, the proof file produced for a reply so the verifier can check it.

entries.meta: A cryptographic proof allowing a verifier to check that a specific reply is what a committed model outputs for a given prompt.
entries.name: Proof of inference
entries.terms: proof of inference a cryptographic proof allowing a verifier to check that a specific reply is what a committed model outputs for a given prompt.

entries.meta: A statement is proved when acceptance by a sound verifier establishes it under the assumptions listed on the claim card.
entries.name: Proved
entries.terms: proved a statement is proved when acceptance by a sound verifier establishes it under the assumptions listed on the claim card.

entries.meta: The software that generates a proof (and, by extension, the party running it).
entries.name: Prover
entries.terms: prover the software that generates a proof (and, by extension, the party running it).

entries.meta: The proving part of a further reply (the further reply less its generation) divided by the serving baseline.
entries.name: Proving vs serving
entries.terms: proving vs serving the proving part of a further reply (the further reply less its generation) divided by the serving baseline.

entries.meta: The organisation that releases a proof system and its documentation, or a model and its weights.
entries.name: Publisher
entries.terms: publisher the organisation that releases a proof system and its documentation, or a model and its weights.

entries.meta: Verbatim quotes copied from a publisher's documentation at the pinned commit, each linked to its exact source lines.
entries.name: The publisher's words
entries.terms: the publisher's words verbatim quotes copied from a publisher's documentation at the pinned commit, each linked to its exact source lines.

entries.meta: Standard 8-bit (Q8_0) and mostly 4-bit (Q4_K_M) quantized copies of the original model, created with llama.cpp at the level's pinned commit.
entries.name: Q8_0 and Q4_K_M
entries.terms: q8_0 and q4_k_m standard 8-bit (q8_0) and mostly 4-bit (q4_k_m) quantized copies of the original model, created with llama.cpp at the level's pinned commit.

entries.meta: Storing a model's weights or activations in fewer bits to make proving cheaper, at the cost of slight numerical drift that can change outputs.
entries.name: Quantization
entries.terms: quantization storing a model's weights or activations in fewer bits to make proving cheaper, at the cost of slight numerical drift that can change outputs.

entries.meta: An idealized hash function that returns a fresh, uniformly random output for every distinct input.
entries.name: Random oracle
entries.terms: random oracle an idealized hash function that returns a fresh, uniformly random output for every distinct input.

entries.meta: A proof that every value in a list fits within a fixed bit width, such as proving each value is below 2^16.
entries.name: Range check
entries.terms: range check a proof that every value in a list fits within a fixed bit width, such as proving each value is below 2^16.

entries.meta: When a glyph grade depends on our interpretation of a publisher's documents rather than a single explicit sentence, the system page marks it with "our reading" and shows the source at the top of the petal's evidence.
entries.name: Read as
entries.terms: read as when a glyph grade depends on our interpretation of a publisher's documents rather than a single explicit sentence, the system page marks it with "our reading" and shows the source at the top of the petal's evidence.

entries.meta: Verifying a model's output by running the model again on trusted hardware and comparing the results.
entries.name: Recomputation
entries.terms: recomputation verifying a model's output by running the model again on trusted hardware and comparing the results.

entries.meta: Whoever makes a decision based on a verifier's verdict, such as a customer, auditor, regulator, or inspectorate.
entries.name: Relying party
entries.terms: relying party whoever makes a decision based on a verifier's verdict, such as a customer, auditor, regulator, or inspectorate.

entries.meta: One of the six entry checks: every proof must cover all reply tokens in the request, and modifying the first, last, or an interior reply token must cause the verifier to reject the proof (rule).
entries.name: Reply check
entries.terms: reply check one of the six entry checks: every proof must cover all reply tokens in the request, and modifying the first, last, or an interior reply token must cause the verifier to reject the proof (rule).

entries.meta: One prompt paired with its expected reply.
entries.name: Request
entries.terms: request one prompt paired with its expected reply.

entries.meta: What a dishonest prover can still get away with even when its proofs pass verification.
entries.name: Residual
entries.terms: residual what a dishonest prover can still get away with even when its proofs pass verification.

entries.meta: One of the six entry checks: we run the publisher's prover as published at the pinned commit across three cold-start sessions, and every reply must receive an accepted proof (rule).
entries.name: Run check
entries.terms: run check one of the six entry checks: we run the publisher's prover as published at the pinned commit across three cold-start sessions, and every reply must receive an accepted proof (rule).

entries.meta: A statistical guarantee obtained by checking a random subset of outputs rather than every reply.
entries.name: Sampled
entries.terms: sampled a statistical guarantee obtained by checking a random subset of outputs rather than every reply.

entries.meta: A bit-length measure of how hard it is for a cheating prover to get a false proof accepted.
entries.name: Security level
entries.terms: security level a bit-length measure of how hard it is for a cheating prover to get a false proof accepted.

entries.meta: The GPU-seconds per reply needed to serve the benchmark request without a proof using the model publisher's release at full load.
entries.name: Serving baseline
entries.terms: serving baseline the gpu-seconds per reply needed to serve the benchmark request without a proof using the model publisher's release at full load.

entries.meta: One cold-start run of a proof system over a single slot's prompts: loading the model, committing to the weights, and proving every reply (120 replies on Llama 4 Maverick, 5 on Llama 3.1 8B).
entries.name: Session
entries.terms: session one cold-start run of a proof system over a single slot's prompts: loading the model, committing to the weights, and proving every reply (120 replies on llama 4 maverick, 5 on llama 3.1 8b).

entries.meta: One of three fixed prompt sets assigned to a model rung.
entries.name: Slot
entries.terms: slot one of three fixed prompt sets assigned to a model rung.

entries.meta: Two broad families of cryptographic proof systems.
entries.name: SNARK and STARK
entries.terms: snark and stark two broad families of cryptographic proof systems.

entries.meta: The property that a verifier rejects proofs of false statements except with a tiny probability bounded by the security level.
entries.name: Soundness
entries.terms: soundness the property that a verifier rejects proofs of false statements except with a tiny probability bounded by the security level.

entries.meta: The publisher's stated upper bound on the probability that a verifier accepts a false proof, which underpins soundness.
entries.name: Soundness error
entries.terms: soundness error the publisher's stated upper bound on the probability that a verifier accepts a false proof, which underpins soundness.

entries.meta: The exact proposition established by an accepted proof.
entries.name: Statement
entries.terms: statement the exact proposition established by an accepted proof.

entries.meta: The portion of a session after its first release group, once proofs are being emitted at an even pace.
entries.name: Steady state
entries.terms: steady state the portion of a session after its first release group, once proofs are being emitted at an even pace.

entries.meta: A system's average is shown above a threshold when our paired sign-flip test across prompts rejects the null at the standard 5 % level (p < 0.05).
entries.name: Shown above
entries.terms: shown above a system's average is shown above a threshold when our paired sign-flip test across prompts rejects the null at the standard 5 % level (p < 0.05).

entries.meta: An interactive protocol that lets a verifier check the sum of a multivariate polynomial over exponentially many points using only a single random evaluation at the end.
entries.name: Sumcheck
entries.terms: sumcheck an interactive protocol that lets a verifier check the sum of a multivariate polynomial over exponentially many points using only a single random evaluation at the end.

entries.meta: A mathematical statement accompanied by a proof.
entries.name: Theorem
entries.terms: theorem a mathematical statement accompanied by a proof.

entries.meta: The basic unit of text a language model processes, typically a word or subword represented as an integer ID.
entries.name: Token
entries.terms: token the basic unit of text a language model processes, typically a word or subword represented as an integer id.

entries.meta: The request's 512 reply tokens divided by the GPU-seconds required for one reply on a single GPU, reported as tokens/s per GPU with the GPU model named.
entries.name: Tokens per second
entries.terms: tokens per second the request's 512 reply tokens divided by the gpu-seconds required for one reply on a single gpu, reported as tokens/s per gpu with the gpu model named.

entries.meta: The glyph petal asking whether verifying a proof relies on trusting anyone's honesty beyond mathematics, such as a setup secret or a hardware vendor's signing key (petal rule).
entries.name: Trust assumptions
entries.terms: trust assumptions the glyph petal asking whether verifying a proof relies on trusting anyone's honesty beyond mathematics, such as a setup secret or a hardware vendor's signing key (petal rule).

entries.meta: A trusted execution environment (TEE) is a hardware-enforced enclave inside a processor that isolates code and memory from the machine's host.
entries.name: Trusted execution environment
entries.terms: trusted execution environment a trusted execution environment (tee) is a hardware-enforced enclave inside a processor that isolates code and memory from the machine's host.

entries.meta: A one-time ceremony that generates public parameters from secret randomness whose knowledge would allow forging proofs (as in KZG polynomial commitments).
entries.name: Trusted setup
entries.terms: trusted setup a one-time ceremony that generates public parameters from secret randomness whose knowledge would allow forging proofs (as in kzg polynomial commitments).

entries.meta: Checking a claim against evidence that holds up even when the claimant has an incentive to cheat.
entries.name: Verification
entries.terms: verification checking a claim against evidence that holds up even when the claimant has an incentive to cheat.

entries.meta: The software that checks a proof against a commitment and prompt, then accepts or rejects it (taking the reply as an input or reading it from the proof).
entries.name: Verifier
entries.terms: verifier the software that checks a proof against a commitment and prompt, then accepts or rejects it (taking the reply as an input or reading it from the proof).

entries.meta: One of the six entry checks: the verifier must reach every verdict with no copy of the model weights on disk and no GPU visible (rule).
entries.name: Verify without weights check
entries.terms: verify without weights check one of the six entry checks: the verifier must reach every verdict with no copy of the model weights on disk and no gpu visible (rule).

entries.meta: The learned numerical parameters that define a neural network, about 8 billion in Llama 3.1 8B.
entries.name: Weights
entries.terms: weights the learned numerical parameters that define a neural network, about 8 billion in llama 3.1 8b.

entries.meta: A measurement scope counting all GPU time in a session from the start of the commit call through the release of the final proof (including commit, generation, and proving, but excluding model loading before commit), divided by the number of replies proved.
entries.name: Whole session
entries.terms: whole session a measurement scope counting all gpu time in a session from the start of the commit call through the release of the final proof (including commit, generation, and proving, but excluding model loading before commit), divided by the number of replies proved.

entries.meta: All private data the prover uses to construct a proof that the verifier never sees.
entries.name: Witness
entries.terms: witness all private data the prover uses to construct a proof that the verifier never sees.

entries.meta: The property that a proof reveals nothing beyond the truth of its statement: everything the verifier sees could be simulated without knowing the model weights.
entries.name: Zero knowledge
entries.terms: zero knowledge the property that a proof reveals nothing beyond the truth of its statement: everything the verifier sees could be simulated without knowing the model weights.
